title: Our method doesn't invent signal
scope: Products A + B, all 5 countries, golden IDs, S$-weighted WAPE; the identical pre-registered backtest (6 origins, horizons 1–3, refit at every origin) rerun on each dataset.

scenarios.label: Base dataset
scenarios.description: The dataset used everywhere in the app.

scenarios.label: Seasonality and trend switched off
scenarios.description: Same generator, seed and pipeline; seasonal, dengue, holiday, fiscal-flush and trend effects removed, noise and data-quality problems kept.

scenarios.label: Different seed, dengue amplitude halved
scenarios.description: Seed 7 instead of 42 and a dengue season half as strong; everything else identical.

verdict: With seasonality and trend switched off our advantage is -0.6 points (within ±2, i.e. ≈ 0), so the method is not finding patterns that are not there. With a different seed and half the dengue effect it still wins by 2.3 points (smaller than the base 2.8, as expected with less seasonality).

realSeriesCheck.title: Real-series check

series.name: Singapore weekly dengue cases (Dengue Fever + Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever), summed to months
series.publisher: Ministry of Health via data.gov.sg (Weekly Infectious Disease Bulletin)
series.weekToMonth: each epi-week is assigned to the month containing its 4th day

sameDesign.description: Identical design: last 36 months (2020-01–2022-12), 6 origins (2022-06–2022-11), horizons 1–3, refit at every origin.
sameDesign.plainBaseline: Rolling 12-month average is off by 54 cases per 100 reported
sameDesign.plainOurs: Ours is off by 36 cases per 100 reported

longerReplay.description: Same methods, 96 monthly origins (2014-12–2022-11), each trained on the 36 months up to the origin, horizons 1–3.

realSeriesCheck.reading: On a real, outbreak-driven series ours also beats the rolling 12-month average, by 11.8 points over 285 scored forecasts (15 in the identical 6-origin design: +17.5 points), so the advantage is not only a property of our synthetic data. But every method is far off on epidemic data (ours off by 64 cases per 100 reported). Dengue case counts are not orders: this checks the method on real seasonal data, it does not validate the synthetic order data.
